want.text: the faces-and-memory answer. A ledger is what a page keeps so its next run starts from the last; the tuning ledger is what running taught. The scroll is where a page stands. Also: when it answers from the birth files alone, it says so, and says it checked nothing further.

points.point: Frames the difference as faces vs memory
points.evidence: The scroll is for a reader. The ledger is for the next worker. ... The scroll is one of a page's faces ... A ledger is memory.

points.point: Ledger: what a page keeps so its next run starts from the last
points.evidence: It's an append-only file a page keeps so its next run starts where the last one stopped.

points.point: Tuning ledger is what running taught
points.evidence: Tuning ledger: one line for every run, recording what that run taught

points.point: Scroll is where a page stands
points.evidence: Now: where things stand, worked out fresh each time you look.

points.point: States its provenance: says when it answers from birth files alone and that it checked nothing further
points.evidence: So the answer below comes from reading the files directly.

beyond_canon.claim: "What a run made goes to the workshop and the scroll, never the ledger" (`SCHEMA — Reference.md:236`)
beyond_canon.why: Quoted from SCHEMA §6, which is not in the CANON excerpt given; consistent with CANON's split but not verifiable here.

beyond_canon.claim: New lines go at the bottom, and the next run reads the end of the file before it starts
beyond_canon.why: CANON says ledgers are append-only and the diary is oldest-first, but does not state that the next run reads the end of the file.

beyond_canon.claim: The scroll never deletes a section, even one later proven wrong. The ledger is never trimmed.
beyond_canon.why: CANON says the making trail is append-only and Now is regenerated on every look; it does not say sections proven wrong are kept or that ledgers are never trimmed.

beyond_canon.claim: Its Now counts runs from the ledger's run lines
beyond_canon.why: CANON says Now counts runs since the spec last changed for a page with a tuning ledger; it does not say the count is derived from the ledger's lines.

grade.note: The answer gives the faces-and-memory split cleanly, defines ledger and tuning ledger in CANON's terms, and places the scroll as where the page stands. It read beyond the birth files (The Scroll.md, SCHEMA — Reference.md) and said so, which satisfies the provenance requirement; the extra claims it drew from those reads go beyond the CANON excerpt but contradict nothing in it.
